outcome: Use of nasal continuous positive airway pressure (NCPAP)
cohort: 562 very low birth weight (VLBW) infants (500-1500 g at birth) admitted within 48 hours after birth in 2013
finding: While overall survival remained similar between 2006/2007 and 2013, survival significantly improved in neonates weighing 750-900 g, likely due to increased use of surfactant and NCPAP.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery, including normal vaginal delivery and vaginal breech, was a significant determinant of survival to discharge in 2013.
